description: The sticky animated navbar and footer (design §2 sections 1 and 9), the full App.jsx composition wiring Backdrop + Navbar + all sections + Footer (§2/§6), and a final integration pass for responsiveness, accessibility, performance, and the three device tiers (§5). Depends on FEAT-001/002/003 (imports every section, the Backdrop, and the hooks). This feature makes the site a complete, runnable single page and must run last.
steps: Create src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx: a fixed <header>; left callsign/name mark (mono), nav links from portfolio.nav as real <a href="#id"> with aria-current active state driven by useActiveSection, and a live mono clock / SYS NOMINAL status chip; transparent at top -> .glass + bottom hud.line border after scroll via Framer Motion useScroll; mobile hamburger <button aria-expanded aria-controls="mobile-menu"> opening a full-screen HUD overlay menu (id="mobile-menu") that uses useFocusTrap (Esc closes and returns focus to the toggle). Smooth-scroll relies on anchors + CSS scroll-behavior.

Create src/components/layout/Footer.jsx: a <footer> mono strip with callsign, '© {year} {name}', 'BUILT WITH REACT · THREE.JS', a back-to-top link (#top), and a faint animated grid baseline (aria-hidden).

Replace src/App.jsx with the §2 composition: <Backdrop/> then <Navbar/> then <main> containing Hero, About, Skills, Experience, Missions, Gallery, Contact (each a <section id aria-labelledby>), then <Footer/>. Leave src/main.jsx and its <React.StrictMode> unchanged. Remove any scratch wiring left from FEAT-001's verification.

Integration pass against design §5: confirm semantic landmarks (header/main/footer, section aria-labelledby, <h2> headings); decorative HUD layers are aria-hidden + pointer-events-none; nav links, mobile menu (open/trap/Esc/focus-return), contact form, and mission expanders are keyboard-reachable with visible focus rings; alt text comes from data (alt="" for placeholders); hud.dim is used only for labels, not body copy. Confirm the Three bundle stays code-split and does not block first paint, and that reduced-motion disables infinite animations + telemetry ticking + Framer loops.

Verify the three device tiers behave: desktop (full canvas + cursor tilt), narrow width or low hardwareConcurrency/deviceMemory (canvas with reduced dpr, parallax off), and prefers-reduced-motion or no-WebGL (StaticHudHero, no canvas). Fix any seams between sections (spacing rhythm, duplicate ids, Backdrop z-index vs content).
Run the final build and a preview smoke check; fix any issues before marking complete.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` exits 0 with the Three.js bundle code-split into its own chunk.
`npm run dev`/`npm run preview` shows the complete single page scrolling through Hero -> About -> Skills -> Experience -> Missions -> Gallery -> Contact -> Footer in order, with no console errors.

The sticky navbar is transparent at top and gains the glass treatment + border after scroll; nav links smooth-scroll and the active link highlights (aria-current) per section; the mobile menu opens, traps focus, and closes on Esc restoring focus to the toggle.
The page is usable by keyboard end to end (nav, mobile menu, contact form, mission expanders) with visible focus; decorative layers are aria-hidden.
The three device tiers render as specified (desktop canvas, downgraded canvas on narrow/low-power, StaticHudHero under reduced-motion/no-WebGL).
verification: Run `npm run build`; confirm exit 0 and a separate three/@react-three chunk in the output.

Run `npm run preview` (or `npm run dev`); scroll the full page at desktop and mobile widths confirming section order, smooth-scroll + active-nav highlight, sticky-navbar glass-on-scroll, mobile menu focus trap + Esc, and zero console errors; with DevTools force prefers-reduced-motion and confirm StaticHudHero + no infinite animation + no telemetry ticking.
